title: A quiet observation at a revision different from the latest source change is accepted silently and leaves the item unable to complete
outcome: A quiet observation at a revision different from the latest source change is accepted silently and leaves the item unable to complete
acceptance: On an unfinished run with no active named root, judged from the recorded claim/run lifecycle, a new admitted observation with source_changed=false and a measured source basis is refused at checkpoint with the typed error execution_observation_source_revision_mismatch naming both revisions when the run's latest effective source-change record at the transactional cut is admitted, measured, in the same workspace and at a different revision. The guard does not compare across workspaces, skip beneath a newer unadmitted change, or invent a missing anchor or revision. The entire checkpoint rolls back; exact committed replay remains unchanged, changed committed intent still conflicts, and an uncommitted key may be retried with corrected input. Named-root behavior and the newest-measured-sighting rule for unadmitted triggers remain unchanged; historical records are read as stored without retrospective reclassification.

a test reproduces the TermAl w-805e92312e06 sequence (a change at revision A, then quiet observations and a passing check at revision B, no named root) and shows the quiet observation at B refused with execution_observation_source_revision_mismatch, with nothing from that checkpoint recorded
behavioral-control-plane.md states what source_changed=false asserts about the revision, so hosts know the contract
